title: m⁶A as a Gatekeeper Linking RNA G-Quadruplex Folding to Stress Granule Condensation: A Hypothesis and Critical Review
content: RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s) and N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A)-binding proteins have both been implicated in stress-granule (SG) biology. Here, we critically examine a conditional mechanism based on the ability of m⁶A to reshape local RNA structure: when a methylated A-U pair contributes to a duplex that competes with an rG4, methylation may weaken that duplex and increase the fraction of RNA adopting the quadruplex. A transcript carrying accessible m⁶A sites and a folded rG4 could then recruit YTHDF readers and rG4-binding proteins, through distinct contacts. The complete sequence from site-specific methylation through rG4 folding to altered SG recruitment has not been demonstrated in cells. However, in vitro studies show recognition of rG4 by METTL3-METTL14 and reduced ALKBH5 demethylation near a G-tetrad, suggesting possible local reinforcement at compatible sites. Other studies report stress-dependent rG4 folding, and effects of m⁶A readers or G-rich RNA on SG behaviour, but their contribution to transcript recruitment remains disputed. We separate these observations from the proposed mechanism, define position- and stress-dependent predictions, and outline biophysical, cellular and reconstitution experiments that could support or falsify the individual steps of this framework.
